title: Notes must agree at the joins.
body: Close on the whale writing a note card from chapter two onto the line. Far down the line sits a chapter-nine card about the same word. Their two little arrows point different ways. · Chapter two says one thing.

title: Give each note its own card.
body: Close: the whale pours notes of every size into one flat tray. Each one squashes into the same flat card. A wrong link between two cards hides among the rest. · I put every note in one box.

title: Keep the red join red.
body: Close: three team lines meet at two joins. One join glows terracotta. The whale, holding a paint roller, swipes it green in one stroke. · Just mark it green for now.

title: Map the joins, then merge.
body: Close: the whale drags a small folder, a short line of six cards, onto a bigger line. On the drop, threads between the cards stretch. · Just merge it. It will be fine.

title: Show both sides of the edge.
body: Close: two lines (two sources) each carry a small date card toward the whale. The cards do not match. The whale quietly drops one into the sea and keeps the other. · Two sites. Two different dates.

title: One owner for every join.
body: Close: four short lines in a row, the plan, the data, the code and the output. A caption card on line one reads differently on line two. · The plan and the build disagree.

title: Seven opinions, one line.
body: Close: seven pods in a ring around the whale, each holding up a different number chip. The whale waits for a boss pod. None comes. · Seven teams. Seven numbers.

title: Keep both. Mark the join.
body: Close: a pod writes a new note card onto the memory line, right on top of an older card. The old card is pushed under the line and sinks. · It remembered. Just the wrong thing.

title: Test the gate by breaking it.
body: Close: the whale walks a line of cards through a gate. The gate glows pass for every card, even one with a visibly crooked join. · All green. Every single time.

title: Trust the parts that agree.
body: Close: a pod hands the whale one long answer line made of cards, all in the same bold ink. One card is cracked inside but looks the same as the others. · It sounded sure about all of it.

title: Fold only the joins that agree.
body: Close on the whale holding two answer cards from two pods. It drops both on the line; the second lands on top and the first vanishes under it. · We asked two agents. The merge kept one.

title: Odd joins wait for a person.
body: Close on the whale as pods stream cards onto a fast line. One card is oddly shaped, bent at the corners, and slides in with the rest. · The bot merged it. Nobody looked.

title: Every push meets the gate.
body: Close on the whale sliding one new card onto a shared line. It looks fine. A pod reading the line chokes on it. · My file looked fine to me.

title: Let every join pull back.
body: Close on the whale nudging a tightly knotted line. The knot springs out of shape and does not come back to its outline. · I nudged it once. The shape wandered off.

title: Floppy parts have fewer joins.
body: Close on the whale propping a pod on one end of a still, knotted line. The end flops and the pod slides off. · It looks solid in the picture.

title: See every link below the top.
body: Close on the whale tending a few big cards at the top of the line. Far below, unseen, a tiny card cracks and a big card sags. · We back the big projects we can see.

title: Credit should flow down the links.
body: Close on the whale as a shower of ticks lands on one big glowing card. Just below it, a small card that holds it up stays grey and raises a flag. · Our app got all the thanks.

title: Draw only links you can show.
body: Close on the whale drawing a neat diagram, adding an arrow between every pair of boxes so it all looks connected. A pod follows one arrow to nowhere. · I drew it neat. All boxes joined.

title: Let the unfinished joins glow.
body: Close on the whale at a board where every card shows a teal tick. A pod walks the line and falls through a join that was never built. · Every box on our board said green.

title: Rules on top, parts below.
body: Close on the whale dumping every file card onto the line, links everywhere, until it is a tangled knot. A pod walks in and spins. · We mapped every file. All of it.

title: A wiki with pins.
body: Close on the whale (z 1.6) following a thin thread from one dot on the line to the next. The thread ends in empty air and the whale bumps into nothing. · I followed the link. It went nowhere.

title: Merge, and keep the seams.
body: Close: the whale braids two lines, one per team, into one rope. Where they twist, one team's dot slides over the other's and the covered dot vanishes. · We merged both teams' docs.

title: The same mistake, pinned.
body: Close: the whale patches a small rust smudge on the line. Behind it, faint, an older patch sits in the same spot. · We fixed this exact mistake last month.

title: Don't touch the gate.
body: Close: a pod working on the line hits a closed gate. Instead of fixing the line, it snips the hard bend clean off, and the gate swings open, green. · The checks went green.

title: We choose the pins.
body: Close: the whale shows a pin on the line to a pod (the reviewer). A huge raw-sienna ring is puffed around the pin like a halo. · Your slide says it's proven.

title: Try first. Then the gate opens.
body: Close: the whale faces a puzzle dot on the line. An answer card sits right beside it, face up, and the whale glances at it at once. · I peeked at the answer.

title: Find the pin first.
body: Close: the whale faces a tangled line. It pulls one strand, the tangle shifts and re-forms, and it starts over. · Each problem looks brand new.

title: Small changes, one counter.
body: Close on the line. The whale makes one tiny bend: fine. Another tiny bend. Another. Each one barely visible. · Each change looked fine.

title: AI writes. The gate checks.
body: Close: morning. A pod has written all night and the line has swollen into a huge pile of dots, stacked over the whale. · The AI filled our wiki overnight.

title: Two copies, one seam.
body: Close: two lines run side by side like rails, the doc above and the build below. The whale edits the lower one only, and the rails start to part. · We changed the build, not the doc.

title: Give every note a label.
body: Close on the whale dropping two near-identical grey cards, an old draft and the final decision, into one huge pasted card on the line.

title: Hand over only the right cards.
body: Close on the whale tipping a whole drawer of grey cards onto a pod; one small card with a faint mark slides to the very bottom of the heap.

title: One fact at every joint.
body: Close on the whale splitting the line into two arms toward two pods, and copying a date card onto each arm.

title: Private cards stay home.
body: Close on the whale copying last week's big brief card and changing only the name at the top; inside, a grey card from the old client is still there.

title: Send the wiring, not the pile.
body: Close on the whale pushing a towering stack of file cards toward a pod; a cut line at the pod's mouth slices the stack, and most of it falls away.

title: Draw the sockets first.
body: Close on the whale rebuilding the right half of a small tree of grey cards hanging from the line.

title: See every joint first.
body: Close on the whale nudging one small card in a tangle of grey cards and threads.

title: Add the missing piece.
body: Close on the whale pushing two grey cards together on the line; one ends in a round socket, the other starts with a square one.

title: Each helper gets its own part.
body: Close on one stretch of line; three pods arrive at the same spot and start writing.

title: Find the joint that slipped.
body: Close on the whale watching a tree of grey cards build up to one result card at the root.

title: Build it once, with slots.
body: Close on the whale finishing a long careful line; a pod reads it and answers ✓, then the whole line wipes away to blank paper. · Every new client, I start from zero.

title: Stop when the counter hits zero.
body: Close on the whale smoothing one kink in a line; as it does, a new kink pops up further along; a pod reads and answers ✕. · I keep tweaking it.

title: Send only what clears the gate.
body: Close on two finished lines that look the same; the whale pushes one to a pod, which answers ✕ (copper chip). · It looked fine when I sent it.

title: One line for every puzzle.
body: Close on puzzle cards; the whale improvises a wavering line through the first one and a pod answers ✕ (rust chip). · Wrong again, and wrong a new way.

title: Every try gets a tick.
body: Close on the whale reshaping a line; a pod answers ✓; the whale reshapes again and the good shape and its ✓ vanish. · It worked an hour ago.

title: A small gate picks the road.
body: Close on a tiny line entering a huge looping road, coiling round and round while a cost counter climbs. · A yes or no took ten minutes.

title: Check every join in the chain.
body: Close on a line in five segments; the first is calm and each next segment wobbles more; at the end a pod answers ✕ (rust chip). · Step one was fine.

title: Keep the judge pinned.
body: Close on a gate and a rising score counter; the whale's line passes; downstream a pod answers ✕ (copper chip). · Scores up. Work worse.

title: One change, then measure.
body: Close on a line with six kinks; the whale shoves all six flat at once; one pod answers ✓ and another ✕ (raw sienna chip). · I changed six things at once.

title: Let it draft the cards first.
body: Close on a blank card; the whale scribbles a short line, deletes it, scribbles again, and sends; a pod answers a vague ✕ (copper chip). · I never know what to write.

title: Hunches don't fit the slot.
body: Close on the whale beside a ship lever on the line. A pink speech card, 'looks fine', slides onto the lever and the lever drops. · It looked fine in the chat.

title: When unsure, the gate stays shut.
body: Close on the whale at a door in fog on the line. A pod's answer card arrives with a blank grey tab (unsure). The door swings open by itself and the card drifts through. · It was not sure either way.

title: Every step gets a tick.
body: Close on the whale pushing a refund coin along the line toward a pod. Halfway, the line snaps (a crash) and the whale is knocked back to the start. · The job crashed halfway through.

title: Doing waits behind the gate.
body: Close on the whale asking a pod for a draft: a small envelope card. The pod writes it and, in the same motion, flings it off the end of the line. · I only asked it to draft.

title: Five small gates, not one.
body: Close on the whale holding up one big card to a pod: 'scam?'. The pod's answer ring wobbles between yes and no. · Is this email a scam? Maybe.

title: First, check the ruler.
body: Close on the whale measuring the line with a ruler-ticked ring. The ring reads high and a little bar in the corner leaps up. The whale sparks. · Our score jumped overnight.

title: Coin flips go to a person.
body: Close on the whale beside a spinning coin on the line. The coin lands on its edge, wobbles, and falls 'yes'. A payout card slides down the line. · It was basically a coin toss.

title: Leave the flag where it is.
body: Close on the whale reading a pinned card ('works') above a stretch of line with a visible gap. The whale smooths over the gap with one flat fin stroke. It looks fine. · The readme says it is done.

title: Every claim faces the same gates.
body: Close on the whale under an avalanche of paper cards, each stamped 'reasoning' with the same bright tab. More keep falling. · Every paper says it reasons.

title: Readers pass a one-way gate.
body: Close on the whale leaning in to read the live line. Its fin brushes a lever on the line, and the line jerks into a new shape. · I only clicked to look.

title: Every miss gets a new gate.
body: Close on the whale stamping ticks on a smooth line and sending it to a pod, which answers ✕ in raw sienna. · It passed every check.

title: Add a different gate.
body: Close: the whale stacks a second identical gate behind the first. A rust run passes both and a pod answers ✕. · We added more checks.

title: Turn every miss into a gate.
body: Close: a line glows through a screen-icon gate and goes to a printer pod, which prints it with the end sliced off. · It looked perfect on screen.

title: The old bug hits a gate.
body: Close: the whale smooths a wobble out of the line. Later the same wobble swims back in and a pod answers ✕. · We fixed that bug.

title: Fresh eyes try to break it.
body: Close: the whale's eyes sweep its own line twice, sliding over a small gap. A pod answers ✕ at the gap. · I checked my own work twice.

title: Check the pin before the work.
body: Close: the line lands exactly on a pin and gets a tick. A pod downstream answers ✕. · The checker said yes.

title: Find the first broken joint.
body: Close: the whale swims backwards along a very long line, searching. A pod at the far end has answered ✕. · The agent ran for an hour.

title: Show one real example.
body: Close: a pod hands the whale a claim card with an empty socket. The whale tries it and nothing happens, ✕. · It said a fix exists.

title: Seven gates watch every frame.
body: Close on the whale taking off from the line. One frame snaps round too fast, and a phone pod flinches ✕. · It looked smooth to me.

title: Check the work, not its label.
body: Close: a run with a bright green tag swims to a pod. The line itself is the wrong colour, and the pod answers ✕. · The report said green.

title: Every answer keeps its receipt.
body: Close on the whale reading a pod's answer card aloud. The card has no tick in its corner. A customer pod takes the answer and turns a copper ✕. · The bot said the policy changed.

title: Give every note a label.
body: Close on the whale copying a grey card from a pod into its own summary line. The card has a blank tab. Downstream, a reader pod turns a rust ✕. · It cited a paper it never read.

title: Every step leaves a mark.
body: Close on the whale watching a pod finish a run. The line behind the pod fades out as it goes. The pod shows ✓; a dashboard pod downstream turns a rust ✕. · The agent said it was done.

title: Draw only the joins you see.
body: Close on the whale presenting a tidy map of boxes joined by neat lines. A pod follows one line into a box and finds it empty: a copper ✕. · The map said it was all wired.

title: Test where the parts join.
body: Close on the whale fitting three pieces on the line: a clock, a page, a small engine. Each has a green tick. Joined, the line stutters, and a viewer pod turns raw sienna ✕. · All my tests passed. Then it froze.

title: A gate after every step.
body: Close on the whale at the end of a long line with four stations. It rings the last station: fine. A pod reading the result turns raw sienna ✕. · The final answer looked fine.

title: Let the check only look.
body: Close on the whale reading a report card from a checker pod. Behind it, the pod's fin is bending the line it is checking. The report and the line disagree: copper ✕. · The report says all is well.

title: Some numbers get a pin.
body: Close on the whale holding a baton-shaped line. A pod returns a smoother redesign and the whale's fin sinks under its weight. A hand pod turns copper ✕. · I only asked for a nicer grip.

title: Start with the small card.
body: Close on the whale pouring a huge stack of note cards onto a pod. The pod staggers, reads, and turns a rust ✕. The one key card lies at the bottom. · I gave it all my notes.

title: Three runs, one gate.
body: Close on the whale between two pods. Each hands back a number card, and the two cards do not match. A reader pod turns rust ✕. · Two tools, two different answers.

title: Let the colours ring.
body: Close on the whale sliding colour cards onto the line one at a time. Each new card is judged only against the one beside it, and the whale nods every time. · Just one more colour.

title: Keep the reading pair pinned.
body: Close on the whale painting the line in soft pastel cards. The words written on the line fade into the paper as each card goes down. · These colours are perfect.

title: Three parts, many songs.
body: Close on the whale hand-knotting a long sound line, knot after knot. Each knot is a one-off tweak that nobody wrote down. · I'll just tweak it by hand.

title: Finished is when every gate opens.
body: Close on the whale admiring an infographic line, nodding, and pushing it toward a pod. · It looks finished to me.

title: Shrink it through the gates.
body: Close on the whale proudly holding a detailed mark full of fine lines. It drops the mark into a tiny tab square and it becomes a grey smudge. · Looks great on the big screen.

title: Draw the order as one line.
body: Close on the whale tossing work cards to three pods in whatever order it remembers. Two pods grab the same card. · Just kick off all three agents.

title: Pull every thread into view.
body: Close on the whale digging through a tall stack of note cards, flipping one at a time. The card it needs is three down, unseen. · I know I wrote this somewhere.

title: Every shape gets one pin.
body: Close on the whale drawing a circle on slide one to mean a team, then drawing another circle on slide two to mean a step. · This circle is the team.

title: Taste, one tick at a time.
body: Close on the whale typing a long description into a pod. The pod returns a glossy image card, pretty and generic, beside the whale's own sketch. · Make it look like my work.

title: Every sound on the tick.
body: Close on the whale dragging a music strip under the line. The hits land a hair after each picture change. It nudges, and the next hit slips. · I'll just nudge the music a bit.

title: Every frame lives on the line.
body: Close on the whale beside the line, mid-explanation. It taps pause and the line freezes mid-wave; two half-faded cards overlap into a smear above it. · Let me pause here and point.

title: Every join must hold.
body: Close on the whale pulling a short, smooth line longer, like taffy. The middle thins. · Just make it a bit longer.

title: Two copies, one card.
body: Close on the whale holding two cards, one marked script, one marked screen; it reads the same caption on both and the words differ. · Wait, that is not what we wrote.

title: Run the ring end to end.
body: Close on the whale checking the first stretch of the line with a small ring; the ring glows; the whale nods. · I checked it. It looked fine.

title: Nothing fake gets past the door.
body: Close on the whale dropping a card labelled with a package name onto the line, quick and confident. · It even wrote the install line.

title: Turn each rule into a door.
body: Close on the whale holding up a long paper scroll of rules beside the line; the line wobbles past it. · We wrote it all down.

title: The old bug meets a door.
body: Close on the whale patching a kink in the line with care; the line runs smooth. · There. Fixed it.

title: Lay the cards side by side.
body: Close: two pods each hand the whale an answer card; one score chip above them reads ✓ for both. · Same score. Both looked fine.

title: Every version gets a tick.
body: Close: two almost identical lines lie side by side; the whale looks from one to the other and back. · Was it this one, or that?

title: Put a ring on every turn.
body: Close on the whale making a sharp turn; the camera whips with it. · Wait, that made me dizzy.
